description: Vector index structures decomposed. HNSW (hierarchical navigable small world). IVF (inverted file). Product quantization. Locality-sensitive hashing. The mechanisms that make approximate nearest neighbor search at billion-vector scale tractable.

sub_mechanisms.name: ANN_approximate_nearest_neighbor
sub_mechanisms.definition: Find k nearest vectors to query within tolerance. Exact NN is O(N) for billion vectors; ANN trades small accuracy loss for log/sub-linear time.
sub_mechanisms.why: Vector search foundation. Recall (fraction of true neighbours returned) vs latency tradeoff. 95-99% recall typical. Standard in RAG, recommendation, image search.

sub_mechanisms.name: HNSW_layered_graph
sub_mechanisms.definition: Hierarchical Navigable Small World: multi-layer graph. Top layer: few sparse-connected nodes. Each layer below: more nodes + more connections.
sub_mechanisms.why: Search descends layers: start at top entry, find closer node, descend. Each layer prunes search exponentially. O(log N) search; high recall.

sub_mechanisms.name: HNSW_M_parameter
sub_mechanisms.definition: Max connections per node. Typical M=16-48. Higher M = better recall, more memory, more build time.
sub_mechanisms.why: Graph density trade-off. Quality scales with M up to ~50. Memory: ~4M bytes per vector for graph (vs vector itself). Standard for production HNSW.

sub_mechanisms.name: HNSW_ef_construction
sub_mechanisms.definition: Search width during graph construction. Higher = better-built graph, slower build, no query-time cost.
sub_mechanisms.why: One-time cost. ef_construction=200 produces high-quality graph; ef_construction=40 is fast but lower quality. Tuned per dataset.

sub_mechanisms.name: HNSW_ef_search
sub_mechanisms.definition: Search width at query time. Higher = better recall, slower query.
sub_mechanisms.why: Per-query latency vs recall trade. ef=10-200 typical. Dynamic: can tune per query for different SLAs.

sub_mechanisms.name: IVF_inverted_file
sub_mechanisms.definition: Cluster vectors via k-means. At query: find nearest cluster centroids; search within those clusters.
sub_mechanisms.why: Older but still common. Smaller memory than HNSW (no graph). Slower than HNSW for same recall. Used in Faiss, IVF-PQ combos.

sub_mechanisms.name: IVF_nprobe
sub_mechanisms.definition: Number of clusters to search per query. More = better recall, slower.
sub_mechanisms.why: Standard IVF tuning. nprobe=1 fast but low recall; nprobe=100 high recall, slow. Per-query knob.

sub_mechanisms.name: product_quantization
sub_mechanisms.definition: Split vector into M sub-vectors; quantize each into K codes. Vector represented as M small ints.
sub_mechanisms.why: Dramatic memory reduction. 1536-dim float vector (6 KB) → 16 bytes (375x smaller). Cost: approximate distances (use lookup tables). Foundation of billion-scale ANN.

sub_mechanisms.name: ScaNN_google
sub_mechanisms.definition: Google's ScaNN: combines tree-based partitioning + asymmetric hashing + reranking. Highest-recall benchmarks.
sub_mechanisms.why: Engineered for max recall at fixed latency. Used inside Google Search vector retrieval. Open source; widely deployed.

sub_mechanisms.name: Annoy_random_projection_tree
sub_mechanisms.definition: Random projection trees: build many trees with random hyperplane splits. Query: descend each tree to leaf set; union.
sub_mechanisms.why: Spotify's original library. Simple, on-disk friendly. Lower recall than HNSW. Less common in modern systems but historically important.

sub_mechanisms.name: filtered_ANN
sub_mechanisms.definition: ANN with predicate filter: 'nearest neighbours where category = X'. Combines vector + scalar filter.
sub_mechanisms.why: Real-world queries combine. Pre-filtering (filter first, ANN in subset): slow if subset small. Post-filtering (ANN, then filter): may not return k. Active research; Qdrant + Weaviate + Pinecone all have strategies.

sub_mechanisms.name: vector_quantization_compression
sub_mechanisms.definition: Reduce vector size: float32 → float16 (2x), int8 (4x), 1-bit (32x). Trade precision for storage.
sub_mechanisms.why: Vector databases store billions of vectors. Compression is key. ANN search uses lookup tables on quantized codes. Binary quantization gaining popularity (10x faster, modest recall loss).

derivation_rules.name: HNSW_log_N_search_via_layered_graph
then: search is O(log N) instead of O(N)
derivation_rules.why: Each layer cuts search space. Top: few entries; bottom: all data. Descend layer by layer. Same insight as skip list, applied to vector space. Foundation of HNSW's performance.

derivation_rules.name: product_quantization_dramatic_memory_reduction
if: vector is split into M sub-vectors with K codes each
then: storage drops from D × 4 bytes (float) to M × log_2(K) bits
derivation_rules.why: 1536-dim × 4 bytes = 6 KB → M=8 × log_2(256) = 8 bytes (compressed by 750x). Distance approximation via lookup. Foundation of billion-scale ANN (Facebook's FAISS PQ).

derivation_rules.name: recall_vs_latency_pareto_frontier
if: a vector index has tunable ef_search or nprobe
then: recall vs latency traces a Pareto frontier
derivation_rules.why: Higher ef = visit more nodes = better recall + higher latency. Production systems pick per query (or per workload). HNSW dominates this frontier for moderate-size datasets; ScaNN for large.

derivation_rules.name: filter_strategy_depends_on_predicate_selectivity
derivation_rules.why: Selective filter → tiny candidate set → exact search feasible. Non-selective filter → most candidates remain → post-filter from ANN. Engines choose per query. Qdrant + Weaviate + Pinecone all implement.

derivation_rules.name: vector_databases_combine_index_types
then: it typically combines an ANN index with secondary indexes
derivation_rules.why: ANN handles vector similarity; secondary indexes handle predicate. Combining requires careful integration (filter while traversing, build separate indexes per filter, etc.). Active engineering area.
